theater: 德蘭士瓦西部與奧蘭治自由邦

battle.name: 第一次波耳戰爭
battle.theater: 德蘭士瓦西部與奧蘭治自由邦
battle.brief: 一八八〇年十二月，德蘭士瓦武裝村民起事，逐走英方守軍，重開人民議恢復共和國。英軍在帕德克勞與英戈戈兩度敗績，一八八一年二月在梅奇山取回主動權，三月佔領布隆方丹，五月簽訂比勒陀利亞協約。雷管步槍是這場戰爭的樞紐：布爾射手伏在丘陵後方五六百碼外單發點射，英軍線形隊形屢次在射程內散開。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries:
大英帝國一方是一個正在改組中的帝國軍隊：駐紮在好望角殖民地與納塔爾的英方部隊，分為常備營（第一與第二營皇家因尼斯金林步槍兵團，第五十八、第二十四與第九十步兵團）、好望角殖民地的民兵與騎槍志願隊、納塔爾的志願兵，以及皇家炮兵與皇家工兵。指揮體系在開局分成三個互不協同的縱隊：一八八〇年十一月由少將喬治·波默羅伊·卡特率領的中央縱隊進駐德蘭士瓦的比勒陀利亞；一八八一年初由少將喬治·貝克率領的德蘭士瓦野戰縱隊負責德蘭士瓦方面；殖民地政府另派旅級軍官阿布思諾特率領的奧蘭治河縱隊進入奧蘭治自由邦。炮兵由各縱隊分帶，野砲與火箭連不歸步兵營指揮，而是按各縱隊需要臨時編配，射擊諸元難以統一，縱隊之間也沒有互相支援的安排。

德蘭士瓦與奧蘭治自由邦一方沒有常備軍。每一個戰鬥單位都是由民眾自發組織的武裝騎兵隊，每名成員自備坐騎、步槍與皮帶彈盒，編制從數十人到數百人不等，由民選的戰地將軍率領，輔以副將與號角傳令，並沒有統一的參謀機構。政權方面，一八八〇年十二月十三日在帕德克勞召開的人民議宣布不承認英方一八七七年的吞併，德蘭士瓦恢復共和國，由馬丁努斯·韋塞爾·普雷托里烏斯主持議會，保羅·克魯格與皮特·朱伯特分任軍事首腦；奧蘭治自由邦另設人民議，由雅各布·德·韋特與克里斯蒂安·弗雷德里克·德·韋特分掌政軍。兩邦在軍事上互相呼應，卻從未合併成一個中央指揮系統。
countriesEn:
The British side was an imperial army in the middle of reorganisation: the troops stationed in the Cape Colony and Natal comprised regular battalions (the first and second battalions of the Royal Inniskilling Fusiliers, the 58th, 24th and 90th Regiments of Foot), the militia and mounted rifle volunteers of the Cape Colony, Natal volunteers, and the Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers. The command structure at the outset was divided into three mutually uncoordinated columns: in November 1880 Major-General George Pomeroy Carter led the Central Force into Pretoria in the Transvaal; in early 1881 Major-General George Beck took over the Transvaal Field Force for the Transvaal theatre; and the colonial government sent a separate column under a brigadier general into the Orange Free State. The artillery travelled with each column, and the field guns and rocket troops were attached ad hoc to the columns rather than commanded by the infantry battalions, so that the gunnery could not be unified in range and target, and there was no arrangement for one column to support another.

The Transvaal and the Orange Free State had no standing army. Every combat unit was a body of armed horsemen raised by the burghers themselves, each man bringing his own horse, rifle and bandolier, organised in companies of a few dozen to a few hundred men, commanded by an elected field general with a second-in-command and horn signals, and with no general staff at all. In political terms, the Volksraad that met at Paardekraal on 13 December 1880 refused to recognise the British annexation of 1877 and restored the republic, with Marthinus Wessel Pretorius presiding over the assembly and Paul Kruger and Piet Joubert heading its military; the Orange Free State kept a separate Volksraad, with Jacob de Wet and Christel de Wet holding the government and the command. The two republics supported one another militarily without ever being merged into a single central command.
people:
保羅·克魯格是這場戰爭最關鍵的人物。他是德蘭士瓦的農場主兼民眾領袖，一八七九年在對祖魯人的戰事中曾率武裝人員挫敗英方的接管企圖；一八八〇年十二月，他率數百名武裝騎兵攻佔英方在海德堡的據點，又在帕德克勞召開人民議、宣讀宣言，宣布不承認英方的吞併。帕德克勞一役實際上由他指揮，他選擇在英軍縱隊行軍路線側翼的丘陵後方佈置射手，等英軍進入開闊地才開火。皮特·朱伯特是德蘭士瓦第一位戰地將軍，在英戈戈一役統率射手，逼迫英軍縱隊投降。雅各布·德·韋特是內閣部長，負責外交與補給；他的堂弟克里斯蒂安·弗雷德里克·德·韋特是奧蘭治自由邦最出色的指揮官，一八八一年三月率武裝隊越過奧蘭治河深入好望角殖民地作戰，並在和談中扮演關鍵角色。馬丁努斯·韋塞爾·普雷托里烏斯以人民議主席身份率領代表團前往比勒陀利亞談判，最後簽下協議。

英方方面，陸軍總司令弗萊德里克·羅伯茨坐鎮倫敦，內閣在格萊斯頓於一八八〇年重新組閣之後對戰事態度搖擺，遠程兵力不足成為各方爭論的焦點。少將喬治·波默羅伊·卡特率中央縱隊進駐德蘭士瓦，屢次求援；少將喬治·貝克於一八八一年二月接掌德蘭士瓦野戰縱隊，在梅奇山策劃攻擊；中校阿蘭·加德納率領的縱隊在帕德克勞被全滅；少校查德在英戈戈被圍後率八十三人投降；少校戴利率領的騎兵小分隊在蘭茲河遭布爾武裝襲擊而退。
peopleEn:
Paul Kruger was the decisive personality of the war. He was a Transvaal farmer and popular leader who in 1879 had led armed burghers to frustrate a British take-over during the war against the Zulus; in December 1880 he took several hundred armed horsemen and seized the British positions at Heidelberg, and then called the Volksraad at Paardekraal and read out the proclamation renouncing the British annexation. He personally directed the fighting at Paardekraal, choosing to place his shooters behind the hills flanking the line of march of the British column and to open fire only once the column had entered the open ground. Piet Joubert was the first field general of the restored Transvaal and commanded the shooters at Ingogo, where he forced a British column to surrender. Jacob de Wet was a member of the ministry and handled foreign affairs and supply; his cousin Christel de Wet was the ablest commander of the Orange Free State, led armed columns across the Orange River into the Cape Colony in March 1881 and played a decisive part in the peace negotiations. Marthinus Wessel Pretorius, presiding over the Volksraad, headed the delegation that went to Pretoria to negotiate, and signed the final agreement.

On the British side the commander in chief Frederick Roberts remained in London, and after Gladstone formed his second government in 1880 the cabinet wavered over the war, with the shortage of troops far from the theatre the chief point at issue. Major-General George Pomeroy Carter led the Central Force into the Transvaal and called for help more than once; Major-General George Beck took over the Transvaal Field Force in February 1881 and planned the attack at Majuba; Lieutenant-Colonel Alan Gardner's column was annihilated at Paardekraal; Major Chard, encircled at Ingogo, surrendered with eighty-three men; and Major Daly's mounted detachment was driven back by Boer irregulars at the Elands River.
kits:
雷管步槍在這場戰爭裡同時是兩邊的武器，而兩邊的用法截然不同。英方一八七九年制式的馬丁尼-亨利步槍採用雷管式落下槍機，由早期滑膛槍改膛線而成，口徑五七七英分，槍身配可折疊的照門，是步兵班的主要火器，可靠射程約在三百至五百碼之間，超過這個距離精度便迅速下降。雷管式的價值在這裡格外明顯：底火不受風雨影響，清晨的濃霧與揚塵中仍然擊發得響，射手不必等到天光大亮才敢開火。

布爾一方大量使用繳獲的英軍雷管步槍，數以千計的馬丁尼-亨利流入各武裝隊手中，同時仍使用自有的長身滑膛步槍與短身卡賓槍，並以皮帶式彈盒在胸前攜帶數十發子彈，備彈由鞍袋與隨身車載供應。射手把步槍架在石頭或自製的射擊棍上，採跪姿單發射擊，命中精度遠高於英軍的整排齊射。

砲兵方面，英方皇家炮兵配九磅與七磅後膛野砲，九磅砲需六匹馬牽引，七磅砲需四匹，另設康格里夫火箭連，英方在比勒陀利亞還配有一挺加特林機槍，起事當日與野砲一同落入布爾方手中；這些砲與火箭在帕德克勞與英戈戈兩度被布爾射手完整繳獲，火箭連的發射架與火箭後來反被布爾方用來對付英軍縱隊。布方只有少量舊式六磅與四磅口徑砲，多半是前次戰爭的戰利品，平時分藏於溝渠。運輸方面，英方依賴好望角至奧蘭治河的鐵路與數百里牛車線，彈藥由前線兵站分發；布方以本地補給為主，糧食自備，行動輕快。
kitsEn:
The percussion rifle was at once the weapon of both sides in this war, and the two used it in completely different ways. The British Martini-Henry rifle, service issue from 1879, used a percussion falling block and had been made by rifling older smoothbore muskets; its calibre was .577 inches and it carried a folding rear sight, and it was the main arm of the infantry section. Its reliable range lay between three hundred and five hundred yards, and beyond that the accuracy fell away quickly. The value of the percussion principle showed itself here with particular clarity: the cap was unaffected by wind and rain, so the weapon still went off in the morning mist and in the dust thrown up by the wagons, and the shooter did not have to wait for full daylight before firing.

The Boer side used large numbers of captured British percussion rifles; thousands of Martini-Henrys found their way into the commandos, who went on using their own long-barrelled smoothbore muskets and short carbines as well, and carried several dozen rounds per man in a bandolier across the chest, with reserve ammunition in the saddlebags and in the wagons. The shooter rested his rifle on a rock or on a shooting stick and fired single shots from the kneeling position, with an accuracy far above that of the British volley at close range.

On the artillery side the Royal Artillery brought nine-pounder and seven-pounder breech-loading field guns, the nine-pounder needing six horses and the seven-pounder four, together with a Congreve rocket troop, and a Gatling gun stood in Pretoria, to be lost with the field guns on the first day of the rising; both the guns and the rockets were captured whole by Boer shooters at Paardekraal and at Ingogo, and the rocket frame and rockets were afterwards turned by the Boers against British columns. The Boers had only a few old six-pounder and four-pounder pieces, mostly spoils of the earlier war, hidden in ditches when not in use. On the transport side the British depended on the railway from Cape Town to the Orange River and on hundreds of miles of ox-wagon road, with ammunition distributed from the advanced depots; the Boers lived off the country, carried their own food and moved lightly.
tactics:
布爾的戰術核心是拒絕接戰、掌握射界與不斷轉移。開戰之初，武裝隊不進攻英軍據點，只在英軍巡邏與縱隊側翼的丘陵後方集結，等英軍進入開闊地再以單發精確射擊招呼之；英軍每推進一段距離，都要花費大量時間搜索正面。帕德克勞的教訓最典型：英軍縱隊在起伏地帶行進，砲隊成了布爾射手的首要目標，砲組人員與挽具大量損失，縱隊隨即潰散。

英軍仍以十九世紀的線形密集隊形與整排齊射為基本教條，因此傷亡極重；一八八一年二月梅奇山之戰，貝克吸取教訓，步兵以稀疏的散兵線前進，砲兵先行射擊，再由左翼三路同時發起攻擊，火箭連在側翼提供火力支援，結果仍以逾一千八百人的代價換取勝利。英軍騎兵多為龍騎兵，戰鬥中要下馬作戰，與步兵的協同不佳；而布爾的每一個武裝隊本身就是全騎兵，展開與收攏只需一次號角，撤退時分批散開再重新集結，令英方難以追擊。英方補給線長達數百里，傷寒與痢疾在沿線營地蔓延；布方糧食自帶，行動半日即可改變方向，這一點是英方無法模仿的。
tacticsEn:
The core of Boer method was to refuse close contact, to hold the field of fire and to keep moving. At the outset the commandos did not assault the British posts; they assembled behind the hills flanking the patrols and the marching columns and greeted the British with single aimed shots once those had entered the open ground, so that every yard the British advanced cost them a great deal of time spent searching the front. The lesson of Paardekraal is the clearest case: a British column was marching across broken ground, the guns became the first target of the Boer shooters, the gun crews and the harness were destroyed, and the column dissolved.

The British still clung to the linear close order and the massed volley as the basis of their infantry doctrine, and the cost was extremely heavy; at Majuba Hill in February 1881 Beck had learnt his lesson and advanced with infantry in thin skirmish order, the artillery firing first, three lines of attack going in simultaneously from the left, with the rocket troop giving fire support on the flank, and the victory was still bought at the price of more than eighteen hundred casualties. The British cavalry consisted largely of dragoons who had to dismount to fight and worked badly in concert with the infantry, whereas every Boer commando was mounted from end to end, expanding and contracting at a single blast of the horn, and breaking away in parties before reassembling, which left the British unable to follow. The British supply line ran for hundreds of miles, and typhoid and dysentery spread along its camps; the Boers carried their own food and could change direction within half a day, and that was something the British could not copy.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰事自一八八〇年十二月的起事算起，至一八八一年五月三日簽訂比勒陀利亞協約，前後約五個月；若連其後的賠償分配程序一起計算，則延續到一八八二年。起事前段，一八八〇年十二月十六日，布爾武裝隊在比勒陀利亞河畔與英軍巡邏交火，攻入皇家酒店，英方丟下兩門野砲與一挺加特林機槍，二十一日撤出城內。帕德克勞一役，英方派出的縱隊約二三百人，結果全軍潰散，損失九磅砲兩門、康格里夫火箭連的發射架與火箭，以及九磅砲彈約六百發。英戈戈一役，英方少校查德率八十三人投降，繳出一門七磅砲與一批火箭及彈藥。梅奇山一役，英方出動約二千人，配野砲九門及火箭連，布方集結約二至三千名武裝騎兵；英軍陣亡三百餘人、受傷近一千五百人，合計逾一千八百，布軍損失為數十人，另有若干被俘。英方在南非的部隊因傷寒與痢疾病倒者達數千人，其中死亡數以百计，遠多於作戰傷亡。德蘭士瓦與奧蘭治自由邦的白人居民各只有數萬，能騎馬上陣者以萬計，兩邦在一八八一年能投入的武裝隊規模因此有限。最終由英方政府支付給陣亡布爾人家屬的賠償，由一個委員會逐案評定，總額達十數萬英鎊，分數次撥付，到一八八四年才結清。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war is counted from the rising of December 1880 to the signing of the Pretoria Convention on 3 May 1881, a matter of about five months; if the subsequent distribution of compensation is included, the business ran on into 1882. Early in the rising, on 16 December 1880, Boer armed parties exchanged fire with a British patrol on the banks of the Spruit at Pretoria and stormed the Royal Hotel, and the British left two field guns and a Gatling gun behind as they cleared the town on the twenty-first. At Paardekraal the British column numbered perhaps two or three hundred men, was completely broken up, and lost two nine-pounder guns, the Congreve rocket frame and rockets, and about six hundred rounds of nine-pounder ammunition. At Ingogo Major Chard surrendered with eighty-three men, giving up a seven-pounder gun together with rockets and ammunition. At Majuba Hill the British committed about two thousand men with nine field guns and a rocket troop, against two to three thousand armed Boer horsemen; British dead numbered over three hundred and wounded nearly fifteen hundred, more than eighteen hundred in all, while Boer losses were a few dozen men with a number taken prisoner. British troops in South Africa were laid low by typhoid and dysentery in the thousands, and the deaths among them ran to hundreds, far more than the combat casualties. The white populations of the Transvaal and the Orange Free State numbered only tens of thousands each, and the number of men who could ride to war was counted in thousands, so the size of the commando that each republic could put into the field in 1881 was limited. The compensation finally paid by the British government to the families of the Boer dead was assessed case by case by a commission, came to well over a hundred thousand pounds sterling, was paid in instalments, and was not wound up until 1884.
cause:
起因是一八七七年英方對德蘭士瓦的吞併，以及隨後在稅收與債務上持續加壓。一八七六年英國內閣在卡那封勳爵推動下決定接管德蘭士瓦，理由是德蘭士瓦未按一八七四年比勒陀利亞協約接受英方提出的仲裁安排，亦未償付欠款；英軍入城後宣布吞併，並在最高法院增設英籍代表，把原本名義上自治的共和國改造成由英方主導的附屬地。一八七七年，奧蘭治自由邦亦被好望角殖民地政府合併。吞併之後，駐節代表以欠款為由年年查封農莊、沒收牲畜，年成稍差便需借貸度日，農民與商人的怨恨逐漸累積。一八七九至一八八〇年，英方以追討欠款為名出動小隊，兩度深入德蘭士瓦境內，燒毀農莊與穀倉、帶走牲畜，德蘭士瓦人民議屢次交涉均無回應。

一八八〇年夏，局勢到達臨界點：憤怒的民眾自行武裝，保羅·克魯格等人四處招募騎手，英方在奧爾尼河附近搜查穀倉又成導火線。十二月六日前後，武裝隊攻佔海德堡與比勒陀利亞外圍的英軍據點，十二月二十一日比勒陀利亞英軍撤走，十二月十三日人民議在帕德克勞集會，宣布不承認英方的接管，恢復共和國的自治；布爾人重拾武裝，對外則以宗主國的名義維持外交形式，戰爭自此爆發。
causeEn:
The cause was the British annexation of the Transvaal in 1877 and the continuing pressure applied afterwards over taxation and debt. In 1876 the British cabinet, pushed by Lord Carnarvon, decided to take over the Transvaal on the ground that the republic had not accepted the arbitration offered by Britain under the Pretoria Convention of 1874 and had not settled the outstanding debts; the troops entered the capital and proclaimed annexation, and the Supreme Court was given additional British representation, so that a republic that had been autonomous in name was turned into a dependency directed from Britain. In 1877 the Orange Free State was likewise absorbed by the government of the Cape Colony. After the annexation the British resident used the question of arrears to sequestrate farms and seize stock year after year, and in a bad season the burghers had to borrow to live, so that the resentment of farmers and traders accumulated steadily. In 1879 and 1880 British columns went twice into the Transvaal in the name of recovering the arrears, burning farms and granaries and taking cattle, and the Transvaal Volksraad petitioned in vain.

In the summer of 1880 the position reached breaking point: the indignant burghers armed themselves, Paul Kruger and others rode about recruiting horsemen, and a British search of grain stores near the Olifants River in August became the spark. Around 6 December armed parties took the British positions at Heidelberg and outside Pretoria; on 21 December the British garrison withdrew from Pretoria; and on 13 December the Volksraad met at Paardekraal and declared that it would not recognise the take-over, restoring the autonomy of the republic. The Boers took up arms again, while keeping up the forms of diplomacy in the name of a suzerain power, and the war began.
impact:
這場戰爭的影響，最深的一層在技術層面。英軍在南非的敗績讓歐洲各國看清一件事：密集線形隊形在有效射程之內已不再是可靠的遮蔽，稀疏的散兵線與精確射擊可以在數百碼外吃掉縱隊。英軍此後的檢討直接催生了裝備與戰術的連串改動：一八八八年制式化的李-梅特福步槍採用毛瑟小口徑與八發彈匣，一八九五年的李-恩菲爾德換上十發彈匣並把照門推到八百碼，到第一次大戰前的短步槍已能一次壓入十發以上，射擊得以連續進行；重機槍也在此際正式納入英軍編制，一九一四年索姆河戰役的連續射擊戰術，源頭正是這幾年在南非得來的教訓。

政治層面的後果更為長久。英方放棄了永久吞併德蘭士瓦的打算，改以比勒陀利亞協約維持宗主權，兩邦的自治得以延續近二十年。但協議中關於英籍居民可以居留與經商、卻不得取得投票權的安排，製造了一個持續存在的怨恨；協議禁止布爾人繳出武器的條款，也被英方視為對叛亂者的縱容。這兩點在一八九〇年代釀成詹納突擊事件，並最終引爆一八九九年的第二次波耳戰爭。帝國地緣也沒有改變：好望角與納塔爾之間仍插著兩塊布爾領土，第二次波耳戰爭中兩邦分屬敵對陣營，說明第一次波耳戰爭的和平只是把矛盾推後了。英國國內則因這場戰爭批評格萊斯頓政府的半途而廢，軍方要求集中兵力一舉殲滅對手的呼聲日益強烈，長期影響了英國的國防政策。
impactEn:
The deepest effect of this war was technical. The defeats suffered by the British in South Africa showed the European armies plainly that the dense linear formation was no longer reliable cover inside effective range, and that thin skirmish order with aimed fire could destroy a column at several hundred yards. The British review that followed produced a whole sequence of changes in equipment and method: the Lee-Metford rifle standardised in 1888 took the small Mauser calibre and an eight-round magazine, the Lee-Enfield of 1895 was given a ten-round magazine and sights carried to eight hundred yards, and by the short magazine rifle with which the army entered the Great War more than ten rounds could be loaded at a time, so that fire could be kept up continuously; the heavy machine gun was brought formally into the British establishment about the same time, and the continuous-fire doctrine of 1914 in the Somme grew directly out of the lessons of these South African years.

The political consequences were longer-lived still. The British abandoned the idea of holding the Transvaal permanently and kept a suzerainty instead, which allowed the autonomy of the two republics to survive for nearly twenty years. But the arrangement in the convention, under which British residents might live and trade yet had no vote, created a standing grievance, and the clause forbidding the Boers to surrender their arms was read in London as indulgence towards rebels. These two points produced the Jameson Raid in the 1890s and finally triggered the Second Boer War in 1899. The imperial geography was unchanged: two Boer territories still lay between the Cape and Natal, and in the Second Boer War the two republics ended up on opposite sides, which showed that the peace of the First Boer War had merely postponed the quarrel. In Britain the war brought criticism of Gladstone's government for abandoning the fight half way, and the demand in the army for concentration and decisive destruction grew ever louder, with lasting effect on British defence policy.
result:
布爾人在戰場上得勝，卻在政治上失敗。梅奇山一役之後，英方集中兵力攻入奧蘭治自由邦，一八八一年三月十三日英軍進入布隆方丹，該邦政府遷往克魯恩斯塔德，四月的主要抵抗結束。一八八一年五月三日，英方代表與德蘭士瓦、奧蘭治自由邦的代表在比勒陀利亞簽訂協約：兩個共和國恢復自治，議會保有立法與行政權力，答應英國提出的若干條件，並由英方支付對陣亡布爾人家屬的賠償；布爾人則承諾效忠英王、允許英籍居民居留經商，並在外交上與英方協商。英軍於一八八一年夏撤出德蘭士瓦，只留下為數不多的駐節人員與武裝警察。

從裝備的結果看，這場戰爭同樣有明確的答案。雷管步槍在布爾人手上發揮的威力，遠勝於它在英軍編制裡的表現：前者是伏在丘陵後方五六百碼外的單發精確射擊，後者是被動挨打的整排齊射；布爾方從英軍手中繳獲的兩門九磅砲、整套火箭連與數千支步槍，事後大多成了布爾武裝的裝備來源。而英方在梅奇山用一千八百人的代價換來的勝利，證明密集線形隊形已無法在這樣的地形與這樣的射手面前存活，此後的改革便由此展開。
resultEn:
The Boers won on the field of battle and lost in politics. After Majuba the British concentrated their force and entered the Orange Free State; on 13 March 1881 the British took Bloemfontein, the government of the republic withdrew to Kroonstad, and the main resistance ended in April. On 3 May 1881 the British representatives and the delegates of the Transvaal and the Orange Free State signed the convention at Pretoria: the two republics recovered their autonomy, the Volksraads kept their legislative and administrative powers, gave certain undertakings to Britain, and Britain undertook to pay compensation to the families of the Boer dead; the Boers in return promised loyalty to the Crown, allowed British residents to reside and trade, and undertook to act with Britain in foreign affairs. The British troops withdrew from the Transvaal during the summer of 1881, leaving behind only a handful of British officials and armed police.

The same question can be answered on the equipment side. The percussion rifle did far more when it was in Boer hands than it did in the British establishment: single aimed shots from behind a hill at five or six hundred yards on one side, the massed volley taking the fire on the other. The two nine-pounder guns, the whole rocket troop and several thousand rifles taken from the British afterwards became, for the most part, the equipment of the Boer commandos. And the victory the British bought at Majuba for eighteen hundred casualties proved that the dense linear formation could no longer survive against this terrain and these shooters, which is where the subsequent reform of the army began.
